European Grocery Stores Hit by Refrigeration Cyberattacks
Publication: November 2, 2026 / 7:45 AM EST / CBS/AFP

Grocery retailers across multiple European nations experienced unexpected temperature surges in cooling systems on November 2, marking the second major incident in less than a month. Chains including Netherlands-based Ahold Delhaize, Belgium's Colruyt, and Swedish retailers ICA and Coop reported the disruptions affecting stores across Belgium, Luxembourg, and Sweden.

The incidents forced stores to discard thousands of pounds of spoiled food. In one Swedish location, an ICA store in Sjobo posted on Facebook that refrigeration units "have been hacked and they set the temperature at 50 degrees" Celsius (approximately 122 degrees Fahrenheit).

Stephan Moelans, CEO of Belgian refrigeration company Sabcobel, told Belgium's Belga news agency that "We began mobilizing technicians at 1 a.m. to get the situation under control." He noted that affected units had their evaporators switched into defrost mode and that "many units would require physical modifications, and that requires investment."

The October cyberattacks on French supermarket chains E. Leclerc, Intermarché, and Cooperative U targeted refrigeration control systems from Danish manufacturer Danfoss. EU food commissioner Christophe Hansen emphasized that "food security requires more attention at all levels," describing the exploitation of networked system vulnerabilities as a new "reality."

No group has claimed responsibility for either series of attacks.
